report:
Uterus with cervix and bilateral adnexa, total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy and omentectomy

The specimen consists of an intact uterus with cervix (165 g, 92 x 58 x 44 mm) with attached right and left fallopian tubes and ovaries from a laparoscopic, robotic-assisted total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The serosa is smooth and glistening. The endometrial cavity (45 mm in length) contains a polypoid tumour measuring 35 x 30 x 12 mm arising from the endometrium (posterior wall and fundus), with invasion to a depth of 6 mm on sectioning where the myometrium measures 18 mm. The lower uterine segment and cervix are unremarkable. The fallopian tubes and ovaries are unremarkable.

(1-4) Tumour, posterior wall, full thickness.
(5) Tumour, fundus.
(6) Anterior wall, full thickness.
(7) Lower uterine segment.
(8-9) Cervix, anterior and posterior.
(10) Right fallopian tube and ovary.
(11) Left fallopian tube and ovary.
(12-13) Right pelvic sentinel lymph nodes (2).
(14) Left pelvic sentinel lymph node (1).

Sections show a serous carcinoma, high grade, measuring 35 mm and arising in the endometrium (posterior wall and fundus). The tumour shows complex papillary and glandular architecture with slit-like spaces, epithelial budding and tufting, lined by cells with marked nuclear pleomorphism, hyperchromasia and prominent nucleoli; hobnail cells are present and mitotic activity is brisk with atypical forms. The tumour invades less than half of the myometrium (6 mm of 18 mm, 33%). Myometrial invasion is by irregular infiltrative glands eliciting a stromal response. Substantial lymphovascular space invasion is present (5 or more vessels). The lower uterine segment and cervix are uninvolved. The serosa is uninvolved. Both fallopian tubes and ovaries are uninvolved. The ectocervical / vaginal cuff margin is uninvolved (closest distance 15 mm). All 12 pelvic lymph nodes are negative for metastatic carcinoma (0/12). Immunohistochemistry shows intact nuclear expression of MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6 and abnormal p53 staining (strong diffuse nuclear overexpression); POLE sequencing shows no exonuclease domain mutation; the molecular class is p53-abnormal.

- Procedure: Total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy; pelvic lymphadenectomy, omentectomy
- Hysterectomy type: Laparoscopic, robotic-assisted
- Specimen integrity: Intact
- Tumour site: Endometrium (posterior wall and fundus)
- Tumour size: 35 mm in greatest dimension (35 x 30 x 12 mm)
- Histologic type: Serous carcinoma
- Histologic grade: High-grade (non-endometrioid carcinoma)
- Mismatch repair (MMR) immunohistochemistry: Intact nuclear expression of MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6
- p53 immunohistochemistry: Abnormal, Overexpression (strong, diffuse nuclear expression)
- POLE status: Wild-type
- Molecular classification: p53-abnormal carcinoma
- Myometrial invasion: Estimated less than 50% myometrial invasion
- Depth of myometrial invasion: 6 mm
- Myometrial thickness: 18 mm
- Percentage of myometrial invasion: 33%
- Adenomyosis: Not identified
- Uterine serosa involvement: Not identified
- Lower uterine segment involvement: Not identified
- Cervical stromal involvement: Not identified
- Other tissue / organ involvement: Not identified
- Lymphovascular invasion: Present, extensive / substantial (5 or more vessels)
- Perineural invasion: Not identified
- Peritoneal / ascitic fluid: Not submitted / unknown
- Ectocervical / vaginal cuff margin: Uninvolved by carcinoma (closest distance 15 mm)
- Parametrial / paracervical margin: Not applicable
- Pelvic lymph nodes: 12 examined; 0 involved
- Para-aortic lymph nodes: No lymph nodes submitted or found
- Distant metastasis: Not identified
- Additional pathologic findings: None
- Pathological stage classification (AJCC 8th edition): pT1a pN0
  - Stage group (if cM0): IA

UTERUS WITH CERVIX AND BILATERAL ADNEXA, total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy and omentectomy - SEROUS CARCINOMA, high grade, invading less than half of the myometrium; substantial lymphovascular space invasion; cervix and adnexa uninvolved; 0 of 12 pelvic lymph nodes involved; molecular class p53abn; pT1a pN0 (AJCC 8th edition), stage IA (if cM0)

The tumour is p53-abnormal on immunohistochemistry and falls within the p53-abnormal (copy-number high) molecular group, which carries an adverse prognosis independent of histotype and stage; multidisciplinary discussion of adjuvant therapy is advised.
